available_assertion.statement: Integral j is equivalent to potential good reduction.
available_assertion.objects: Elliptic E over the complete discretely valued field K with valuation ring R.
available_assertion.hypotheses: The elliptic-curve local-field setup of VII; for the proof used here the residue characteristic is not2.
available_assertion.parameter_range: The application uses K finite over Q_q, q odd.
available_assertion.uniformity: The required finite extension may depend on E.
available_assertion.constants: No bound on extension degree is used.
available_assertion.normalizations: j is the usual elliptic invariant, not j/1728; integral means j in R.
available_assertion.exceptional_cases: Residue characteristic3 is included; the characteristic2 Appendix proof is not used.
available_assertion.limit_order: Choose a finite extension for each curve, then their finite compositum.

needed_assertion.statement: Every curve in the fixed finite CM diagram has a good model over one common finite extension.
needed_assertion.objects: The curves, arrows, labelled O-actions and level data of Section1.
needed_assertion.hypotheses: Separate CM j-integrality and finite definition fields; q odd.
needed_assertion.quantifiers: Each finite diagram, with arbitrary finite enlargement.
needed_assertion.parameter_range: Integral ideals a prime to qN; complete number-field local fields.
needed_assertion.uniformity: Common extension depends on the finite diagram; no bound over all ideals or torsion orders.
needed_assertion.constants: Finitely many extensions and their compositum.
needed_assertion.normalizations: The chosen reduction place and CM labels are kept.
needed_assertion.exceptional_cases: No one finite field containing all torsion is asserted; no supersingularity conclusion.
needed_assertion.limit_order: Define the finite diagram and action generators before choosing the common extension.

applications.connecting_derivation: Use integral j curve by curve, finite compositum, and base change of smooth proper models.

available_assertion.statement: A smooth proper model of an abelian variety over a connected Dedekind scheme carries the extending abelian-scheme group structure.
available_assertion.objects: A_K and its smooth proper S-model A.
available_assertion.hypotheses: S connected Dedekind, fraction field K, A_K an abelian variety.
available_assertion.uniformity: Unique extending structure as used by the Neron property.
available_assertion.normalizations: Generic group identity and operation are the prescribed ones.
available_assertion.exceptional_cases: A model without smoothness or properness is outside this assertion.

needed_assertion.statement: The common smooth proper elliptic models are elliptic schemes.
needed_assertion.hypotheses: R complete DVR; smooth proper models of the given elliptic curves.
needed_assertion.quantifiers: Every model in the finite diagram.
needed_assertion.normalizations: The same generic group laws and zero sections.
needed_assertion.exceptional_cases: No group law is invented on a singular model.
needed_assertion.limit_order: First choose the common good models, then the extending group structures.

applications.connecting_derivation: Spec(R) is connected Dedekind; apply the proposition to each smooth proper model.

available_assertion.statement: An abelian scheme over a Dedekind base has unique extension of every generic morphism from every smooth source.
available_assertion.objects: Abelian scheme B/S, smooth Y/S and morphism Y_K->B_K.
available_assertion.quantifiers: Every smooth source Y and every generic morphism.
available_assertion.uniformity: Uniqueness holds for all the maps and product-source relations considered.
available_assertion.normalizations: The assertion is the full Neron mapping property, not just extension of sections.
available_assertion.exceptional_cases: BLR proof uses Weil4.4/1; that published transitive input is retained.

needed_assertion.statement: The labelled actions, homomorphisms, compositions and identities in the diagram extend compatibly.
needed_assertion.objects: A,B,A x_R A and their generic maps.
needed_assertion.hypotheses: Both models are abelian schemes; each source used is smooth.
needed_assertion.quantifiers: Every endomorphism in O and every selected arrow; every group-law relation.
needed_assertion.constants: A finite Z-generating set defines the full O-action.
needed_assertion.normalizations: All O labels are retained pointwise.
needed_assertion.exceptional_cases: No appeal only to extension of sections; no claim for nonsmooth source schemes.
needed_assertion.limit_order: Extend maps, then use uniqueness on products to establish all relations.

applications.connecting_derivation: Apply the universal property to the smooth sources A and A x A; relations agree on the generic fiber.

available_assertion.statement: A nonconstant elliptic isogeny f has a unique dual, with both composites multiplication by deg(f); deg[n]=n^2 in every characteristic.
available_assertion.hypotheses: f nonconstant; field setting of III.6.
available_assertion.quantifiers: Every such f and every integer n.
available_assertion.parameter_range: Generic and special fields; n may be divisible by the characteristic.
available_assertion.uniformity: The identities are exact, without a separability restriction on [n].
available_assertion.normalizations: The dual reverses the arrow; degree is the scheme-theoretic degree.
available_assertion.exceptional_cases: The zero morphism is not used as a nonconstant isogeny; published errata directions/signs retained.

needed_assertion.statement: Reduction is injective on O; dual identities persist for the actual ideal isogeny.
needed_assertion.objects: Labelled alpha in O and degree-d ideal isogeny f.
needed_assertion.hypotheses: Nonzero alpha acts nontrivially generically; extension of the dual and identities by CJR-EXTENSION.
needed_assertion.quantifiers: Every alpha in O and every selected f.
needed_assertion.parameter_range: No q-coprimality needed for injectivity; d prime to qN in the ideal application.
needed_assertion.uniformity: Pointwise injectivity for the same labelled action.
needed_assertion.normalizations: The dual is defined over K by uniqueness and Galois invariance.
needed_assertion.exceptional_cases: No reduction of degree modulo q; [q] is still a nonconstant morphism.
needed_assertion.limit_order: Extend identities before taking the special fiber.

applications.connecting_derivation: If a nonzero alpha reduced to zero, its dual composite [m] would reduce to zero, contradicting the positive degree formula.

available_assertion.statement: A map between smooth S-schemes is etale at x when its relative cotangent map after extension to k(x) is an isomorphism.
available_assertion.objects: g:X->Y, X and Y locally of finite presentation over S.
available_assertion.hypotheses: X smooth at x; the cotangent condition of17.11.2(c′); in our use both structural maps are smooth.
available_assertion.uniformity: Pointwise criterion, applied at all points.
available_assertion.normalizations: Use pullback of relative differentials; optional tangent condition(d) has an extra residue-field hypothesis.
available_assertion.exceptional_cases: Do not assume k(x)=k(y); do not use a criterion only over a field.

needed_assertion.statement: [n] and the selected f are etale over R.
needed_assertion.objects: Maps of the good elliptic schemes.
needed_assertion.hypotheses: n prime to q; for f, dual composites are[d] with d prime to q.
needed_assertion.parameter_range: Rank-one relative tangent bundles; finite-presentation models.
needed_assertion.uniformity: Translation transports the identity differential to all geometric points.
needed_assertion.constants: The differentials multiply to the unit d; d[n] is multiplication by n.
needed_assertion.normalizations: The tangent/cotangent maps are relative to R.
needed_assertion.limit_order: Differentiate group identities, then apply the cotangent criterion.

applications.connecting_derivation: The differential is a unit on the rank-one tangent bundle; the source and target are smooth over R.

available_assertion.statement: An etale morphism is locally quasi-finite; a proper quasi-finite morphism to a locally noetherian scheme is finite.
available_assertion.objects: Morphisms of schemes with the stated base conditions.
available_assertion.hypotheses: For local quasi-finiteness use EGAIV17.6.2; for finiteness the target is locally noetherian and the map proper.
available_assertion.uniformity: Exact finiteness, with no quantitative bound.
available_assertion.normalizations: Quasi-finite includes quasi-compactness here; proper implies finite type.
available_assertion.exceptional_cases: Proper alone does not imply finite; the etale/quasi-finite step is essential.

needed_assertion.statement: [n], f and their kernels are finite etale.
needed_assertion.objects: Maps in CJR-JACOBIAN and their zero-fiber kernels.
needed_assertion.hypotheses: Proper elliptic source, separated elliptic target, R noetherian, and the proved etaleness.

available_assertion.statement: A finite etale morphism is finite locally free; its rank is locally constant.
available_assertion.quantifiers: Every such f and point of Y.
available_assertion.uniformity: Rank constant on each connected component.
available_assertion.constants: Rank equals the geometric fiber cardinality for an etale map.
available_assertion.normalizations: Rank is not reduced modulo the residue characteristic.
available_assertion.exceptional_cases: Connectedness must be established before claiming one global degree.

available_assertion.statement: Finite etale algebras over a henselian local ring are equivalent to finite etale algebras over its residue field.

available_assertion.quantifiers: Every finite etale algebra and every map.

available_assertion.uniformity: Full faithfulness preserves every selected diagram and endomorphism.
available_assertion.normalizations: Geometric points require a chosen geometric specialization.
available_assertion.exceptional_cases: The statement does not apply to arbitrary finite non-etale algebras.
available_assertion.limit_order: Pass to strict henselization after proving finite etaleness; then compare the same components.

local_derivations.statement: The finite etale special map represents the quotient by its computed kernel, by the explicit torsor identity.
Bezout on N-torsion, compatible d-inverses on q-primary kernels, and differentiation of O-equivariance preserve the stated labels.
